subject: ss-pulmonology
title: Occupational and environmental lung disease: dusts, asbestos and sensitisers

steps.tx: A detailed **occupational history** is the single most important diagnostic step and must cover hobbies, home exposures, secondhand smoke and nearby industry. Include short and long term exposures from the distant past, school years and military service, since **latency** can stretch over decades before symptoms appear.
steps.say: The exposure history carries the greatest diagnostic weight in lung disease clinics. Hobbies and home exposures are also important in clinic practice today. Distant exposures are still relevant because latency stretches over decades for patients.

steps.tx: Inorganic dusts typically cause **interstitial fibrosis** with a restrictive pattern and reduced diffusing capacity on function tests. Dusts and chemicals that provoke **occupational asthma** or COPD instead cause airway obstruction, and a fall in **FEV1** across a work shift detects an acute bronchoconstrictive response to the workplace.
steps.say: Fibrosing dusts cause restriction with reduced diffusing capacity on tests performed. Sensitising exposures cause obstruction instead of restriction in workers daily. A fall in FEV1 across one shift suggests occupational asthma clearly in workers.

steps.tx: **Silicosis** shows small rounded opacities on chest radiograph, while **asbestosis** favours small linear and irregular opacities, graded with the **ILO classification** for pneumoconiosis screening. CT and high resolution CT detect subtle opacities, pleural thickening and interstitial change more sensitively than plain films.
steps.say: Rounded opacities suggest silicosis while linear opacities suggest asbestosis in workers. The ILO scale grades screening films for pneumoconiosis in surveys conducted. CT detects change earlier than plain radiographs do in practice for patients.

steps.tx: Silica impairs **alveolar macrophage** function, so silicosis raises risk of mycobacterial, atypical mycobacterial and fungal infection including tuberculosis. Complicated disease means nodules reaching **1 cm** or more, coalescing into **progressive massive fibrosis** with severe restrictive and obstructive impairment and premature mortality.
steps.say: Silica impairs macrophage killing of mycobacteria inside alveoli daily in workers. Nodules of one centimetre or more define complicated silicosis cases in practice. Progressive massive fibrosis causes severe impairment and early death in workers.

steps.tx: **Asbestos** causes a spectrum from benign effusions and pleural plaques to asbestosis, bronchogenic lung cancer and **mesothelioma** of pleura or peritoneum. More than **80 percent** of mesotheliomas relate to asbestos, with latency up to **40 years**, while lung cancer latency spans about **15 to 19 years** after first exposure.
steps.say: Asbestos causes plaques, fibrosis, lung cancer and mesothelioma in workers daily. Over eighty percent of mesotheliomas follow asbestos exposure in series reported. Latency can reach forty years for mesothelioma cases diagnosed late in life.

steps.tx: Smoking and asbestos interact more than additively, and lung cancer risk exceeds the sum of either exposure alone. **Mesothelioma** risk, however, shows no association with smoking, and **pleural plaques** by themselves imply only past exposure without pulmonary impairment even when films look dramatic in an individual worker.
steps.say: Smoking plus asbestos multiplies lung cancer risk substantially in cohorts studied. Mesothelioma risk owes nothing to smoking history in patients with exposure. Plaques alone signal exposure rather than impairment in most workers screened.

steps.tx: **Chronic beryllium disease** mimics sarcoidosis with noncaseating granulomas, and the distinguishing test is the **beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test** showing a specific cell mediated response to beryllium. **Farmer lung** hypersensitivity pneumonitis presents **4 to 8 hours** after heavy exposure with fever, chills and malaise that mimic influenza or pneumonia.
steps.say: Beryllium disease imitates sarcoidosis clinically and radiologically in exams for students. The lymphocyte proliferation test separates the two conditions well in practice. Farmer lung fevers occur four to eight hours after exposure in workers daily.

steps.tx: **Caplan syndrome** combines pneumoconiotic nodules with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis and was first described in coal miners. **Acute silicosis** follows very heavy short exposure such as sandblasting or artificial stone fabrication, resembles alveolar proteinosis with crazy paving, and can progress severely even after exposure stops.
steps.say: Caplan syndrome pairs pneumoconiotic nodules with rheumatoid arthritis in miners evaluated. Acute silicosis follows heavy short exposure in workshops quickly in patients. Disease can worsen even after exposure stops completely in patients.

steps.tx: No specific drug therapy reverses **asbestosis**, and care remains supportive as for any diffuse interstitial fibrosis with exposure removal and smoking cessation. **Latent tuberculosis** merits longer treatment in silicosis, and documented mesothelioma after asbestos exposure may be **compensable** for affected workers and families seeking justice.
steps.say: Asbestosis has no specific drug and care stays supportive always in practice. Silicosis patients need longer latent tuberculosis therapy for control in clinics. Mesothelioma after asbestos may be compensable under law for families affected.

steps.tx: High yield anchors: exposure history is the top diagnostic step, eggshell nodes occur in about **20 percent** of silicosis, asbestos lung cancer latency is **15 to 19 years**, mesothelioma latency reaches **40 years**, over **80 percent** of mesotheliomas follow asbestos, farmer lung arrives **4 to 8 hours** after exposure, **beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test** separates beryllium disease from sarcoidosis, and plaques alone mean exposure only.
steps.say: Exposure history is the single most important diagnostic step in practice for students. Eggshell nodes appear in about one fifth of silicosis cases recorded. Asbestos latencies extend for decades after exposure to asbestos fibres daily.

rows: Over 80 percent asbestos related, latency to 40 years
